# OpenProgram 1.5.1 Release Notes

OpenProgram 1.5.1 reaches your computer from a phone or another computer, with Tailscale built in; lets a chat run on Codex; turns applications into packages that hold their own conversations and export as software of their own; adds a screenshot tool, a Review pane and Browser Annotate; and updates itself in the background. Which packages this release carries is listed under "Download and installation".

## ✨ New features

- **Devices and remote access.** Settings → Devices is one list of computers, servers and phones. Add device shows a one-time QR code and link for a phone, connects another OpenProgram, an SSH host from `~/.ssh/config`, or takes a sentence for the agent. A phone connects on the same Wi-Fi or from anywhere through the built-in Tailscale, also behind a system proxy. A paired device stays signed in until it is revoked or idle for 30 days.
- **OpenProgram on a phone.** The web UI is a one-column app on a phone: the sidebar is a swipe-in drawer, the right panel a full-screen sheet, and the composer stays above the keyboard. It can go on the Home Screen, and this computer sends it notifications when a conversation needs you, a reply is ready or a conversation stops with an error.
- **Chats on Codex.** A Harness chip before the model chip hands a conversation's turns to the Codex you installed, one Codex thread per branch, with its commands, edits and searches shown in the reply. The model menu lists the models a newer Codex brings and offers **Update Codex**. Settings → Third-Party Harnesses shows what Claude Code and Codex on this computer use and what it would cost at API prices.
- **Applications as packages.** An application can hold conversations of its own, with your composer where it asks, send messages as you, and set the composer's hint. Meetings is now such a package. `openprogram programs export`, or **Export as an application of its own…** on the Applications page, writes a macOS app or a folder that runs the application by itself. Auto Research ships as an example application.
- **Take a screenshot from anywhere.** Freeze the screen, pick a window or area, mark it up, then copy, save, pin, read its text or send it to the chat.
- **Review pane.** Unstaged and Staged scopes with Stage and Unstage, line comments that go to the agent together, and **Review with agent**, which can be stopped and survives a dropped connection.
- **Browser Annotate.** In the desktop App's Browser tab, click an element or drag a box to pin a numbered note, try Size, Spacing and Color on the live page, and send all notes to the chat with a screenshot.
- **Computer use by device.** `computer_use` picks a device and then a window, the screen or a browser. It drives Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Arc, Chromium, Chrome and Edge channels, Safari and Firefox, runs on Linux Wayland, and can operate a paired computer once its owner allows it. The whole screen stays off until you turn it on. A tab can hold another application's window.
- **Projects on any machine.** "Open folder on…" picks the machine first, then the folder, and the project's conversations run there.
- **Tasks and Activity.** Tasks, at the top of the sidebar, has an Inbox of what always-on Agents and scheduled tasks left for you and a Scheduled tab as a list or calendar. Activity draws a conversation's work as one chart from topics to messages, steps and sub-agents, each saying what it is doing and for how long; the sidebar bell lists the last week's running, waiting, failed or unread conversations.
- **Updates in the background.** A new release downloads by itself and waits behind a NEW badge beside the wordmark; **Restart to update** installs it and opens the new version.
- **Office files.** A Word, PowerPoint or Excel file a reply sends shows its first page on its card, and closing a file with unsaved changes asks Save, Don't Save or Cancel.

## 🐞 Bug fixes

- **Long conversations keep going.** Every request is sized by one rule and made to fit the context window before it is sent, so a long conversation no longer stops because its context "does not fit"; automatic compaction measures the request a turn sends, and a compacted conversation keeps showing its original messages.
- **Credentials.** An API key is stored once per company and listed on every way that takes it, each way keeping its own state for it; a request whose way refused every key is sent through another way that accepts one. The quota of Codex, DeepSeek, MiniMax's Token Plan and OpenCode Go is read from the provider.
- **Grok with Search** no longer fails with "Duplicate tool names: web_search".
- **Stopping a run** always stops the command its turn started.
- **Markdown** written in Chinese renders as written, and a link to a local file whose path has a space in it is a link again.
- **Office files** are never written when nobody changed them, and an editor that read a deck or workbook with slides or sheets missing stays read-only.
- **Pages never fail whole.** Saving an MCP server that the server refuses, or opening a step on the Activity chart, says what went wrong in place instead of replacing the window.
- **Other fixes.** A retry of a reply that is only an error takes that turn's place; the App no longer jumps in front of the app you are in while the Agent works in its browser; a tool call still running reads as running.

## 🚀 Improvements

- **No more Loading… or Retry.** Pages, Settings, the right panel and conversations show what they read last at once and refresh quietly behind it; pages are fetched ahead of the click.
- **Nothing polls on a timer.** The Worker and the windows learn of changes as they happen, and an idle Worker reads, parses and checks far less: a Worker start no longer reads every conversation, memory use is lower, and a session log is read a line at a time.
- **Faster opening.** A long conversation's context ring is ready in a fifth of a second, its resources read in 25 ms instead of 330, and every page makes fewer requests as it opens.
- **Smaller downloads.** A runtime ships one Chromium, one Node and no leftover wheel, the Claude Agent SDK is no longer a dependency, and the bundled docs site is smaller.
- **A new look for choices and surfaces.** Every choice among a few is one groove with a sliding face; Settings is grouped into Personal, Models and abilities, Computers and connections, and Data; provider cards show one row per credential with its limits; the side menu collapses without redrawing its rows.
- **The slash menu** is the same popover as the @ menu, with an icon on every row, and @ lists every web page in the conversation's Resources.
- **The new-tab launcher** pages and makes folders as Launchpad does, with a mouse wheel and by dragging.
- **The website** at fzkuji.github.io/OpenProgram is a download page with a product tour video.

On macOS, open the DMG and copy `OpenProgram.app` to `/Applications`. On Windows, run the installer; it installs for your user only. The release manifest lists the SHA-256 of every file. A file whose name ends in `-unsigned` was built without a publisher signature; see "Unsigned packages" below when that applies.

### CLI / Server

Install this release on macOS or Linux; the installer selects the architecture and verifies the runtime:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fzkuji.github.io/OpenProgram/install | OPENPROGRAM_VERSION=1.5.1 sh
```

On Windows x64, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://fzkuji.github.io/OpenProgram/install.ps1 | iex
```

## 🔄 Upgrade guide

- **Desktop, from 1.4.0:** the App finds 1.5.1 when it checks for updates. From this version on, a new release downloads in the background and **Restart to update** beside the NEW badge installs it.
- **Desktop, from 1.3.0 or earlier:** download the package above and install it over the existing App once; an App of 1.3.0 or earlier looks for updates in the repository it was built in.
- **Desktop on macOS:** open the DMG and replace the application in `/Applications`.
- **Desktop on Linux:** install the AppImage or deb above in place of the old one.
- **Desktop on Windows:** run the installer above; it installs over the existing App and keeps your data.
- **CLI / Server:** run `openprogram upgrade`, or repeat the versioned installation command above.
- **Your data:** configuration, conversations, Programs, and saved progress under `~/.openprogram` are preserved.
- **After upgrading:** check `openprogram --version`.

See the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Fzkuji/OpenProgram/blob/v1.5.1/docs/install/upgrade.html) for details.
